approved: Customs Tariff Amendment (Incorporation of Proposals) Bill (No. 1) 2026

Sue Lines I'll now deal with the Customs Tariff Amendment (Incorporation of Proposals) Bill (No. 1) 2026. I'll begin with the second reading amendment circulated by One Nation. The question is that the amendment on sheet 3919 be agreed to. _One Nation_ _'s circulated amendments—_ At the end of the motion, add ", but the Senate: (a) notes that: (i) the Australian timber market is becoming a dumping ground for inferior timber, often from China and containing Russian timber, (ii) the timber industry is Australia's sixth largest manufacturing sector, (iii) Australian timber jobs and businesses, primarily located in regional areas, are at risk from this dumping of inferior imported timber, and (iv) Australia is in the middle of a housing crisis and COVID-19 showed that we cannot rely on imported timber, demonstrating the need for Australia to become self-sufficient in timber and wood products; and (b) calls on the Government to: (i) protect the Australian timber industry from dumped imports; and (ii) introduce country of origin labelling so Australians can make an informed choice about where their timber comes from".

Moved that the Customs Tariff Amendment (Incorporation of Proposals) Bill (No. 1) 2026 be read a second time, outlining duty reductions for almost 500 tariff classifications, extensions of additional duties on Russian and Belarusian goods and free treatment for most Ukrainian goods, plus technical amendments.

Declared that, unless otherwise ordered, the Regulatory Reform Omnibus Bill and Customs Tariff Amendment (Incorporation of Proposals) Bill (No. 1) stand referred to the Federation Chamber after adjournment of debate on their second-reading motions.

Supported the Customs Tariff Amendment (Incorporation of Proposals) Bill (No. 1) 2026, saying it would modernise tariffs, abolish nuisance tariffs across about 500 classifications, extend additional duties on goods from Russia and Belarus, and continue duty-free treatment for Ukrainian goods. Later questioned the bill's scrutiny and called for a Senate inquiry before the question was agreed to.

As President, put the question on a One Nation second reading amendment to the Customs Tariff Amendment (Incorporation of Proposals) Bill (No. 1) 2026 that called on the government to protect the Australian timber industry, Australia's sixth largest manufacturing sector, from dumped Chinese and Russian timber and introduce country-of-origin labelling, before the bill was read a third time and passed.
